title: Hold a spring-return drawer open while retrieving an enclosed block
context: Self-closing drawers in tool chests, parts cabinets and dispensing units shut themselves under a return spring. Taking a part from the rear of one means holding the drawer open with one hand while the other reaches in; letting go while the part or a hand is still in the cabinet mouth closes the drawer on it. The task asks a dual-arm robot to take the block out and shelve it without letting the drawer close on it, then leave the drawer closed.
instruction: Take the white block out of the cabinet and put it on the green shelf, without letting the drawer close on anything, then leave the drawer closed.
setup: All positions are cm from the midpoint between arm bases (x forward, y left); table top is z = 0 (0.7475 m in the simulator world frame). Cabinet: 22.0 x 16.0 x 8.0 cm open-front shell at (41.5, 0.0) with front face at x = 30.5 cm, 1.9 cm birch plywood side walls, 1.5 cm back, 1.0 cm floor and 8.0 kg total mass (steel ballast plate under the floor, rubber feet, friction 1.0, not bolted down). A 2.0 cm thick plywood cover plate covers the rear half (x >= 38.0 cm), its bottom face 6.0 cm above the table. Drawer: 19.0 x 12.0 x 3.0 cm open-top box, 1.0 cm HDPE walls and 0.6 cm floor, 0.40 kg, running on two ball-bearing runners with hard stops at 0 and 14.0 cm, closed with its front face at x = 30.5 cm. Return spring: steel extension spring, 18 N/m, zero preload when closed, anchored between the cabinet back wall and the drawer rear wall, in parallel with a 5 N s/m oil damper. Handle: 2.5 x 6.0 x 3.5 cm aluminium block bolted to the drawer front, centre at (29.25, 0.0). White block: 4.0 cm ABS cube with a 3 mm silicone skin, 0.10 kg, friction 0.8, resting upright and axis-aligned on the drawer floor under the cover plate with its centre at (45.0, 0.0), 3.7 cm above the table surface (z = 0.7845 m in the world frame). A 2.5 cm cyan marker lamp on the cover plate at (45.0, 0.0) is shown when drawer displacement is >= 9.0 cm. Green shelf: 13.0 x 13.0 x 1.0 cm aluminium plate with a rubber top pad, 3.0 kg, friction 1.0, clamped to the table at (30.0, -28.0).
scoring: Score of the current step (end-state; the score never keeps a best value). 0.25 when the drawer has been open >= 9.0 cm for a total of 1.0 s; 0.50 when the white block has been lifted >= 3.0 cm clear of the drawer floor while it was open; 0.75 when the block is resting on the green shelf now (centre within 6.5 cm of the shelf centre in x and y and within 2.0 cm of resting height); 1.00 when, in addition, the drawer is closed (<= 0.5 cm), both grippers are open and both arms are clear (no arm point within 6.0 cm in front of the cabinet face or within 5.0 cm of its width) and still (< 5 mm/s, < 0.2 rad/s), held for 20 control steps (1.0 s at 20 Hz). Zero-gates, latched for the rest of the run: PINCH when the drawer is < 3.0 cm out while the block is still within 6.0 cm behind the cabinet front face; the block falling below the table. The start state scores 0.0.
reset_notes: Verify the spring drawer is fully closed (< 0.5 cm). Confirm the white block rests upright on the drawer floor at (45.0, 0.0) under the cover plate. Verify the cyan open lamp is off and the green shelf is clear.
fidelity: Rigid cabinet, shelf and block with the masses and friction in the setup. The drawer is a real prismatic slider (18 N/m return spring, 140 mm travel, 5 N s/m damping), so it closes when released. In software: the cyan lamp is a marker, the pinch is a position rule on the block (no force is computed), and lifted/on-shelf are position checks. Real build: self-closing parts drawer, bench-top scale, softer spring so the simulated arms can pull it.
